flashcards.q: Bitcoin block header fields and total size?
flashcards.a: 80 bytes: version(4) + prev_hash(32) + merkle_root(32) + timestamp(4) + bits/target(4) + nonce(4). Transactions live in the body, committed via the Merkle root.

flashcards.q: Three validation layers for a new block?
flashcards.a: 1) Structural: parse, size limits, Merkle root, PoW meets target. 2) Contextual: parent linkage, height/difficulty epoch rules, timestamp tolerance (~2h), coinbase subsidy. 3) Execution: full replay of every tx against state (sigs, UTXO/nonce).
Every 2016 blocks (~2 weeks): new_target = old * actual_time / expected_time, clamped to x4 //4 max adjustment. Feedback controller keeping ~10 min blocks under hashpower drift.

flashcards.q: Bitcoin fork choice rule - precise statement?
flashcards.a: Most cumulative WORK, not longest chain. Work per block ~ expected hashes; toy model: leading zero hex digits d -> work = 16^d per block.

flashcards.q: Probability an attacker q=10% of hashrate catches up from z blocks behind?
flashcards.a: ~(q/p)^z: z=6 gives ~0.24%, z=12 ~6e-4. This exponential decay is the quantitative basis for confirmation policies.

flashcards.q: What CAN a 51% attacker do? What CANNOT they do?
flashcards.a: Can: censor txs, reorder recent history, double-spend THEIR OWN coins via private fork release. Cannot: steal others' keys, mint beyond schedule, change protocol rules, revert PoS finality without >=1/3 stake slashed.
12 s slots, 32 slots/epoch (~6.4 min), finality after 2 epochs (~12.8 min). Fork choice attn-GHOST on attestation weight; Casper FFG justifies then finalizes checkpoints.

BTC accidental split Mar 2013: ~6h two chains, 24 blocks orphaned (LevelDB vs BerkeleyDB). Bitcoin Gold May 2018: $18M, ~86-block reorg. ETC Jul-Nov 2020: four attacks, reorgs of ~3.4k-5.3k blocks using rented hashrate.

flashcards.q: Why is a tokenless private chain usually pointless?
flashcards.a: No security budget: either one operator runs it (database with extra steps) or goodwill secures it (collapses - we.trade shut 2022, TradeLens wound down early 2023). Replication paid by incentives IS the security.

flashcards.q: What does assume-valid trust in Bitcoin Core sync?
flashcards.a: That historical blocks below a community-published hash contain valid signatures; script/structure/state still verify. Opt-out exists; drops initial sync from days to hours.

BTC ~7 tx/s base layer; ETH ~15-20 tx/s pre-blobs (higher post-Fusaka blob scaling); Visa peaks ~65k tps. Every full node re-executes everything, so L1 capacity = cheapest acceptable node hardware's capacity.
~120-175 TWh/year (Cambridge index range 2023-2025), comparable to a mid-size country - indefensible for non-monetary use cases.
